svg.title: Plague & Rebellion: Arrival of the Black Death (1348) & The Peasants’ Revolt (1381)
svg.desc: Two-panel KS3 Year 7 historical GIS atlas map: the left main panel shows seamlessly welded medieval Europe and unpartitioned Britain and Ireland with 1347–49 Black Death merchant shipping lanes from Sicily, Genoa, Marseille, Bordeaux, and Calais into Melcombe Regis (Weymouth) in June 1348 and north to Bristol, London, York, and Scotland; the right zoomed Thames Estuary and London GIS inset charts the May–June 1381 Peasants’ Revolt marches from Brentwood in Essex and Maidstone and Blackheath in Kent to Mile End and Smithfield, London.

g.text: 1347–50 BLACK DEATH TRADE ROUTES INTO BRITAIN
ZOOM: MAY–JUNE 1381 PEASANTS’ REVOLT — ESSEX & KENT MARCH ON LONDON
Plague Sweep Across England, Wales & Scotland (1348–50)
1381 Essex Rebels (Brentwood Poll Tax Spark → Mile End)
1381 Kent Rebels (Wat Tyler & John Ball → Blackheath)
Key Turning Points of Plague & Revolt (1–4)
Trade Ships, Melcombe Regis, Rebel Marches & Smithfield

text.tspan: Fleaborne plague travels west on galleys & Gascon ships
Plague enters England; ~40% die, sparking labour shortage
Essex & Kent Poll Tax rebels march under Tyler & Ball
Richard II confronts rebels; Tyler killed, serfdom crumbles

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 7 ENQUIRY: MEDIEVAL ENGLAND (1066–1381)
Plague & Rebellion: The Black Death (1348) & Peasants’ Revolt (1381)
Entering Melcombe Regis in June 1348, the Black Death killed around 40% of England’s people—creating a huge peasant labour shortage.
Frozen wages (1351) and three Poll Taxes sparked the June 1381 march on London; Wat Tyler fell at Smithfield, but serfdom steadily crumbled.
